blocks.md:
Up to now, you spoke in single clauses: *“I ate. I watched a movie.”*

To connect two actions or descriptions with **“and”**, simply attach **-고** directly to the verb or adjective stem. No vowel harmony, no batchim exceptions!

**The Golden Rule of Tense with -고**:

When telling a story in the past, **only conjugate the very last verb into past tense!**

❌ 밥을 **먹었고** 영화를 **봤어요**.
⭕ 밥을 **먹고** 영화를 **봤어요**. *(I ate a meal and watched a movie.)*

items.tip: The room is spacious and clean. (넓다 + -고)
I ate food and drank coffee. (먹다 + -고)
I study Korean and meet my friend. (공부하다 + -고)

blocks.q: How do you combine “방이 넓다 (room is big)” and “깨끗하다 (clean)” with “and”?
blocks.why: Simply attach -고 to the stem 넓-: 넓- + -고 = 넓고.

blocks.meaning: I read a book and went to bed yesterday.
blocks.why: Remember: tense only goes on the final verb (잤어요), so the connector is simply 읽고.

blocks.q: Put in order: "I ate breakfast and went to school."

blocks.hint: Do not put -었- on both verbs! Only the last verb carries the tense.
blocks.why: In a sentence joined by -고, past tense -았/었- only goes on the final verb: 밥을 먹고 영화를 봤어요.

blocks.q: The room is clean and quiet.

blocks.md:
To link two opposing clauses with **“but”** or **“however”**, attach **-지만** directly to the stem.

Just like **-고**, there are no irregular vowel changes: simply glue **-지만** straight onto the stem.

blocks.q: How do you say "This bag is expensive, but pretty"? (비싸다 = expensive, 예쁘다 = pretty)

blocks.meaning: Korean food is spicy, but delicious.
blocks.why: 맵다 + -지만 = 맵지만 (It is spicy, but delicious).

blocks.q: Put in order: "Korean is difficult, but really fun."

blocks.hint: Attach -지만 directly to 춥다 stem: 춥- + -지만
blocks.why: Simply attach -지만 directly to the verb stem: 춥지만.

title.ko: 3강. 어간에 바로 붙이기: 받침과 품사별 꼴
title.en: Lesson 3. Attaching Directly: Verb, Adjective, and Noun Forms

blocks.h: No Batchim Changes: Attach Directly to the Stem
blocks.md:
The best part about **-고** and **-지만** is that they are completely regular!

Whether a stem ends in a vowel or a consonant (받침), whether it's an irregular verb or not, you simply drop **다** and attach **-고** or **-지만** directly to the stem.

For nouns, use **-(이)고** and **-(이)지만**:
- Ends in vowel: 의사**고** / 의사**지만**
- Ends in consonant: 학생**이고** / 학생**이지만**
Notice that irregular verbs like **듣다** (ㄷ irregular) and **춥다** (ㅂ irregular) do NOT change before **-고** or **-지만**. They keep their base stem: **듣고**, **듣지만**, **춥고**, **춥지만**!

items.tip: I listen to music and read the paper in the morning. (듣다 + 고)
It is cold outside, but warm inside the room. (춥다 + 지만)
I am a student, and my sibling is an office worker. (학생 + 이고)

blocks.q: How do you attach ‘-지만’ to ‘듣다’ (to listen)?
blocks.why: -지만 attaches directly to the stem without irregular sound changes: 듣 + 지만 → **듣지만**.

blocks.q: How do you combine ‘선생님’ (teacher, ends in consonant ㅁ) with ‘-고’?
blocks.why: Nouns with a final consonant attach -이고: 선생님 + 이고 → **선생님이고**.

blocks.q: Match each word stem with its correct connected form.

blocks.meaning: The wind blows, but the weather is clear.
blocks.why: Attach -지만 directly to the stem 불- (불다): 불 + 지만 → **불지만**.

blocks.q: Attach -고 to 돕다 (to help) without irregular changes: 「친구를 ___ 청소했어요.」
blocks.why: 돕다 attaches -고 directly to the base stem 돕- without changing ㅂ to 우: **돕고**.

blocks.say: 밖은 춥지만 방 안은 따뜻하고 좋아요.

blocks.q: Read aloud combining both -지만 and -고 smoothly.

title.en: Lesson 4. Choosing Between Connection (-고) and Contrast (-지만)

blocks.h: Connecting Same Direction vs Contrasting Different Directions
blocks.md:
How do you choose between **-고** and **-지만**?

- **-고 (And):** Used when two facts go in the **same direction**:
  - Positive + Positive: "The room is clean **and** quiet" (방이 깨끗하**고** 조용해요).
  - Negative + Negative: "The food is expensive **and** bad" (비싸**고** 맛없어요).
- **-지만 (But):** Used when two facts **contrast** or clash:
  - Negative + Positive: "It is expensive, **but** delicious" (비싸**지만** 맛있어요).
  - Expectation vs Reality: "I studied a lot, **but** the test was hard" (열심히 공부했**지만** 어려웠어요).

blocks.md: Past tense check! In Korean, the past tense marker **-았/었-** can attach before **-지만** (예: 비가 왔지만 갔어요), but for **-고**, the past tense is usually marked only at the very end of the sentence (예: 밥을 먹고 영화를 봤어요).

items.tip: The library is quiet and cool. (Both positive → -고)
There is a lot of work, but it is interesting. (Challenging + positive → -지만)
My sibling is tall, and/whereas I am short. (Contrast in traits)

blocks.q: Which connector fits best: 「이 신발은 편해요. 그리고 가벼워요.」 → 「이 신발은 편___ 가벼워요.」?
blocks.why: Both traits are positive (comfortable + light), so use connection: **편하고**.

blocks.q: Which connector fits best: 「가격은 조금 비싸요. 그렇지만 품질이 좋아요.」?
blocks.why: Expensive (minus) vs high quality (plus) is a contrast, so use -지만: **비싸지만**.

blocks.q: Put the pieces in order: “Korean is difficult, but fun.”

blocks.meaning: Yesterday it rained, but today it is clear.
blocks.why: Past tense 오- + -았- = 왔-. With contrast -지만, it becomes **왔지만**.

blocks.q: Combine 크다 (to be big) and -지만: 「이 방은 ___ 혼자 써요.」
blocks.why: Attach -지만 directly to stem 크-: 크 + 지만 → **크지만**.
